title.narrative: In 2025, UNICEF supported Tajikistan's education system with nationwide shift to competency-based and quality inclusive education by realigning policies, standards, and curricula toward learner-centered approaches and measurable outcomes. The reform delivered revised education standards, updated curricula, formative assessment tools, improved teaching materials, and structured professional development for grades 5-6 across pre-service and in-service institutions, moving classroom practice from rote learning to active engagement with critical thinking and practical skills. Teachers and mentors strengthened their instructional capacity through targeted Continuous Professional Learning courses that enable students to build deeper understanding and transferable competencies, while new adolescent skills modules and a national digital career guidance platform expanded access to educational and vocational opportunities nationwide. These integrated reforms establish scalable infrastructure for sustainable quality improvement, equipping all learners with the cognitive abilities, practical skills, and agency needed for productive participation in society.
